title: Flexbox
summary: Flexbox arranges a group of boxes in a row or a column. It can share space and line up the boxes.
introduction: Flexbox arranges a group of boxes in a row or a column. It can share space and line up the boxes. Picture a row of cards on a desk. Use flexbox to give them a gap, centre them or let them wrap to the next row.
learningObjectives: Create a flex container and control its direction and wrapping
Align and distribute items with justify-content, align-items and gap
Size items with flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis

blocks.text: A flex container and its two axes

`display: flex` on a parent turns its direct children into **flex items** and lays them out along the **main axis**, horizontal by default. The perpendicular direction is the **cross axis**. Three things change immediately: the items sit side by side, they shrink to fit their content instead of stretching across the container, and their margins stop collapsing. Everything else in flexbox is a way of distributing space along one of the two axes.

blocks.text: Distributing items along the main axis: justify-content

`justify-content` decides what happens to the free space along the main axis. `flex-start` (the default) packs items at the start, `center` in the middle, `flex-end` at the end; `space-between` puts the first and last items at the edges and spreads the rest; `space-around` and `space-evenly` add space around every item. A navigation bar is `space-between` in one line.

blocks.text: Aligning on the cross axis: align-items and align-self

`align-items` positions items on the cross axis. The default `stretch` makes every item as tall as the tallest one, which gives you equal-height columns for free. `center`, `flex-start`, `flex-end` and `baseline` do what their names say, and `align-self` overrides the value for a single item. Combine `justify-content: center` with `align-items: center` and you have the famous one-rule centring recipe.

blocks.code: Centred both ways

blocks.text: `gap` puts space *between* items only, with no stray margin at the edges; prefer it to margins on the items. By default all items stay on one line and shrink to fit; `flex-wrap: wrap` lets them move onto new lines instead. `flex-direction: column` switches the main axis to vertical, after which `justify-content` works vertically and `align-items` horizontally. `flex-flow` is the shorthand for direction and wrap together.

blocks.text: Three properties per item control sizing. `flex-basis` is the starting size (`auto` means "use the width, or the content"). `flex-grow` is the item's share of any *free* space: with `flex-grow: 1` on every item they share it equally, with `2` on one item it gets twice as much. `flex-shrink` (default `1`) is the share of the *overflow* taken away when items do not fit. The `flex` shorthand sets all three, and its keywords are what you will actually write.

blocks.text: `min-width: 0` on the growing item matters more than it looks: flex items refuse to shrink below their minimum content size, so a long URL or a wide table inside `.main` would otherwise push the layout out of its container. Setting the minimum to zero lets the item shrink and its content wrap or scroll.

blocks.title: Items shrink unless you tell them not to
blocks.text: Giving a flex item `width: 300px` and finding it narrower is not a bug: `flex-shrink` defaults to `1`, so when the items do not fit, every one gives up some width. Use `flex: none` (or `flex-shrink: 0`) on items that must keep their size, and let one item with `flex: 1` absorb the difference.

blocks.title: Flexbox or grid?
blocks.text: Flexbox distributes items along one line (that may wrap); the items decide the sizes. Grid defines rows *and* columns first and places items into them. Navigation bars, button groups and centring are flexbox jobs; page layouts and galleries are [Grid](/tutorials/css/grid) jobs. Most pages use both.

questions.question: In a row flex container, which property centres the items vertically?
questions.explanation: The cross axis of a row container is vertical, and `align-items` aligns items on the cross axis. `justify-content` works along the main (horizontal) axis.

questions.question: `flex-___: wrap;` lets flex items move onto additional lines when they do not fit.
questions.explanation: `flex-wrap: wrap` allows multiple lines; the default `nowrap` keeps everything on one line and shrinks the items instead.
